meanings.note: Common masculine noun meaning 'bar, pub' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: Our bar is closing.

examples.text: Проверьте все бары и старых друзей.
examples.trans: Check all the bars and old friends.
It is already morning. Our bar is closing.

meanings.note: Privative prefix 'бес-' ('without, -less', before voiceless consonants) (stem 'покоиться'). Reflexive/intransitive verb with the postfix '-ся'/'-сь' (historically from the reflexive pronoun 'себя', oneself). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to worry', paired with 'забеспокоиться'.

examples.trans: Don't worry.
Mum is worried.

examples.text: Это хорошо, что готово. А то мы уже начали беспокоиться.
examples.trans: It's good that it's ready. We were starting to worry.

meanings.note: the present tense is normally left out: я мэр = I am the mayor
present есть; у меня есть = I have

examples.trans: I have a toy car.
Childhood was hard.
You will be asking for forgiveness.
How is it in Hungary?
I grew up in a communal flat.
Hello! How was it in Hungary?
There, look.
Here's my toy car.
All right, here you go. There, look.

meanings.en: to fit in, blend into a team or setting
meanings.note: integrate smoothly into a social group or environment

examples.trans: You fit into the team perfectly.

examples.text: Новичок быстро вписался в рабочий ритм.
examples.trans: The newcomer quickly blended into the work rhythm.

examples.text: Похоже, ты отлично вписываешься в коллектив!
examples.trans: Looks like you fit right into the team!
This is my second term.
The second lesson is hard.

examples.text: Я очень люблю наш город. Поэтому я иду на второй срок.
examples.trans: I love our town very much. That's why I'm running for a second term.

meanings.note: polite to one person, or to several people

meanings.en: other forms: вас (gen/acc), вам (dat), вами (instr), вас (prep)

examples.trans: As you all know...
Does the governor support you?

examples.text: Спасибо, спасибо! Как вы все знаете, я родился и вырос в Синеозерске.
examples.trans: Thank you, thank you! As you all know, I was born and grew up in Sineozersk.

meanings.note: neuter главное, used as a noun
neuter главное, used as a noun

examples.trans: The main thing is, don't worry.
This is the main street.
The most important thing is the people.

meanings.note: at home, a party, or a restaurant

examples.trans: All the guests love them very much.

examples.text: Сегодня вечером к нам придут гости.
examples.trans: Guests are coming to our place tonight.
You have visitors!

meanings.note: на днях = in the next few days, or the other day

examples.trans: Good afternoon!
I'll call in the next few days.
Any day now, on the website.

meanings.note: plural only: there is no singular in everyday use

examples.trans: I have no money.
The money is on the table.
Gum? I didn't have enough money.
A noisy fight broke out on the street.
Stop this senseless fight!
Stop this fight right now!
Thank you for your trust!
Thanks for the present.

examples.text: А сегодня тебя чуть не застрелили!
examples.trans: And today you were almost shot!

examples.text: К счастью, пистолет оказался не настоящим.
examples.trans: Fortunately, the gun turned out not to be real.

meanings.note: to run for a second term

examples.trans: I'm going home.

examples.text: Я очень люблю наш город. Поэтому я иду на второй срок.
examples.trans: I love our town very much. That's why I'm running for a second term.

examples.trans: Let's sum up the first week.

examples.text: В итоге все остались очень довольны.
examples.trans: In the end everyone remained very satisfied.

examples.text: Подведём итоги твоей первой рабочей недели.
examples.trans: Let us sum up your first work week.

meanings.note: all the people working together in an organisation

examples.trans: The staff forced me into this.

examples.text: У нас на работе очень дружный коллектив.
examples.trans: We have a very friendly team at work.

examples.text: Я своё мнение не менял. Это меня коллектив заставил.

Three rooms and a big kitchen.
And the kitchen is over there.

meanings.note: нас = us (gen/acc/prep); у нас = we have, at our place

meanings.en: other forms: нас (gen/acc), нам (dat), нами (instr), нас (prep)

examples.trans: We've done a lot.

examples.text: Смотрите, какой у нас грязный унитаз!

meanings.en: much, far, a lot (before a comparative)
meanings.note: намного хуже = much worse; намного лучше = much better

examples.trans: In prison it will be much worse.
Today is much warmer.

examples.text: Но я же вижу, как тебе плохо. В тюрьме будет намного хуже, поверь мне.
examples.trans: But I can see how bad things are for you. In prison it will be much worse, believe me.

meanings.note: Prefix 'на-' marks surface contact, accumulation, or completing a quantity (stem 'стоящий'). Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('real, genuine').

examples.trans: This is real success!
He is a true friend.

examples.text: Ваня, да пойми ты наконец! Это настоящий успех.
examples.trans: Vanya, understand at last! This is real success.

meanings.note: наш, наша, наше, наши; agrees with the noun

examples.trans: I love our town.
This is our flat.

examples.text: Я очень люблю наш город. Поэтому я иду на второй срок.
examples.trans: I love our town very much. That's why I'm running for a second term.

meanings.note: goes right before the word it negates

examples.trans: I don't know.
There wasn't enough money.
Chef, I didn't take it.

meanings.note: неделю = for a week; через неделю = in a week

examples.trans: I've been waiting a week.
The sea in a week!

examples.text: Меня уже тошнит от этой коммуналки! У нас труба уже неделю течёт.
examples.trans: I'm sick of this communal flat! Our pipe has been leaking for a week now.

meanings.note: trouble or disturbance caused to others

examples.trans: Sorry for the inconvenience caused.

examples.text: Шум в зале создал большие неудобства.
examples.trans: The noise in the dining room caused great inconvenience.

examples.text: Вот вам щедрые деньги за эти неудобства.
examples.trans: Here is generous money for these inconveniences.

meanings.note: + dative of the person: обещать вам

examples.trans: I promise you.
You promised!

examples.text: Марина, я вам обещаю: со стеной ничего не случится.
examples.trans: Marina, I promise you: nothing will happen to the wall.

meanings.note: playful derogatory nickname used by Chef Barinov for Max

examples.trans: Runt, are you still standing here?

examples.text: Огузок, ты официально принят в штат нашего ресторана!
examples.trans: Rump, you are officially hired onto our restaurant staff!

meanings.note: used as an exclamation of approval

examples.trans: I know this town really well!
Everything went great.
Perfect, Vanya!

meanings.en: to poison, intoxicate with venom or toxic substance

examples.text: В первый день ты чуть не отравил гостя.
examples.trans: On the first day you almost poisoned a guest.

meanings.note: с первого раза = the first time

examples.trans: This is my first day.

examples.text: Ты не понимаешь с первого раза?
examples.trans: You don't understand the first time?

examples.text: Ты что, с первого раза не понимаешь?
examples.trans: What, you don't understand the first time?

meanings.note: Common masculine noun meaning 'pistol, handgun' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: Stop, why did you take a pistol?

examples.text: Стой, ты зачем пистолет взял? Ты что, с ума сошёл? Дай сюда!
examples.trans: Stop, why did you take a pistol? Are you out of your mind? Give it here!
I will never let you down.

examples.text: Надёжный друг никогда не подведёт в беде.
examples.trans: A reliable friend will never let you down in trouble.

examples.text: Подведём итоги твоей первой рабочей недели.
examples.trans: Let us sum up your first work week.

Can I go and have a look?
Maybe you could help?
Of course I'll help.

examples.text: Экскаваторщик — это не мой уровень. Может, поможешь?
examples.trans: Excavator driver isn't my level. Maybe you could help?

meanings.note: очень похоже = that's just like him

examples.trans: That's just like him!
It looks like rain.

examples.text: Правда похоже. А может, вы сами позвоните губернатору?
examples.trans: It really is. Why don't you call the governor yourself?
Just like that?
Go straight along this street.

examples.text: В смысле, Виктор Степанович? Прямо так, да?
examples.trans: What do you mean, Viktor Stepanovich? Just like that?

meanings.note: работать + instrumental = to work as: работать мэром

examples.trans: I work as mayor.
Where do you work?

examples.text: Я уже четыре года работаю мэром.
examples.trans: I've been working as mayor for four years now.
That means thousands of jobs.
A working day.

examples.text: Мы построим кластер. Это тысячи рабочих мест.
examples.trans: We will build the cluster. That means thousands of jobs.

meanings.note: short form only: рад, рада, радо, рады; no long-form cases

examples.trans: I'm very glad to see you.
She's glad.

examples.text: Ну что ты? Я очень рад тебя видеть.
examples.trans: Oh, come on! I'm very glad to see you.

examples.text: Его резкие слова сильно разозлили шефа.
examples.trans: His sharp words infuriated the chef greatly.

I'll be there tonight.

examples.text: Виктор Степанович, сегодня никак не могу.
examples.trans: Viktor Stepanovich, I really can't today.
I'm in the office now.
I'll be right there.

examples.text: Конечно, помогу. Кто у вас сейчас начальник?
examples.trans: Of course I'll help. Who's your boss now?

meanings.note: comparative of скоро used as adverb or particle

examples.trans: Let's go quickly to the studio!

Bring the clothespin quickly!

meanings.note: спасибо за + accusative = thank you for

examples.trans: Thanks, Dad!
Thank you for your trust!

examples.text: Спасибо, спасибо! Как вы все знаете, я родился и вырос в Синеозерске.
examples.trans: Thank you, thank you! As you all know, I was born and grew up in Sineozersk.

Come here!
The white one? Give me the keys.

examples.text: Я бы на твоём месте подумал.
examples.trans: If I were you, I'd think about it.
Your boss is here.

meanings.en: other forms: тебя (gen/acc), тебе (dat), тобой (instr), тебе (prep)

examples.trans: You're greedy!
Have you got any more?
Dad, did you bring any gum?
You're fired!
He was fired.

examples.text: Давай мы его уволим, а тебя на его место назначим.

meanings.en: to arrange, organize, set up an event or scheme

examples.text: Я всё устрою на высшем уровне.
examples.trans: I will arrange everything at the highest level.

To cause disturbances.

meanings.note: Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('good, nice').

examples.trans: A good day.

examples.text: Какое хорошее утро! Лидия Алексеевна, чашку кофе, пожалуйста.
examples.trans: What a lovely morning! Lidia Alekseyevna, a cup of coffee, please.
I want coffee.

They want to build a shopping centre there.

meanings.note: чуть не + verb: я чуть не упал = I nearly fell

examples.trans: I nearly fell.
Wait a little.

examples.text: Садись, не бойся. Я ведь сам чуть тебя не отпустил.
examples.trans: Sit down, don't be afraid. I very nearly let you go myself.
Cleverly thought out, boss!
The boss signed the order.
The chef is in the kitchen.

meanings.note: Common substantive noun meaning 'noise' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Ты можешь убрать весь этот шум?
examples.trans: Can you cut out all this noise?
Where is this noise coming from?

examples.text: Так, ты можешь убрать весь этот шум? Нам нужен только Аникеев.
examples.trans: Right, can you cut out all this noise? We only need Anikeev.
You are a very generous person.
Thank you for the generous gift.

examples.text: Извините, вы очень щедрый, а я неловкий. Я пойду попробую приготовить себе кашу.
examples.trans: Forgive me, you are very generous, and I am clumsy. I will go try to cook myself some porridge.

meanings.note: alone: 'я этого не хочу' = I don't want that

examples.trans: This house.
I'm sick of this communal flat.

examples.text: Меня уже тошнит от этой коммуналки! У нас труба уже неделю течёт.
examples.trans: I'm sick of this communal flat! Our pipe has been leaking for a week now.

meanings.en: other forms: меня (gen/acc), мне (dat), мной (instr), мне (prep)

examples.trans: I'm doing my homework.
